findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the mutation-verification step in a platform-neutral form (e.g. run the RED oracle directly under `pytest`, optionally sandboxed) so the WAIT_AND_RETRY-reintroduction mutation check reproduces on Linux/Windows/BSD, not only under macOS `sandbox-exec`.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Mutation check run inside `sandbox-exec -f` (the `timeout` binary is absent on this host): re-introduce `WAIT_AND_RETRY` into the failover set, confirm the oracle goes RED, restore.'
sandbox-exec is a macOS-specific sandbox utility not present on Linux/Windows/BSD.
findings.finding: The Testing section prescribes the mutation verification be run 'inside sandbox-exec -f' — sandbox-exec is a macOS-only binary. A reviewer or CI runner reproducing the mutation check on Linux/Windows cannot invoke sandbox-exec, so the plan's stated mutation-verification methodology does not reproduce off macOS.
findings.location: Testing section — 'Mutation check run inside sandbox-exec -f (the timeout binary is absent on this host)'
scenarios: Platform=Linux CI (any provider) or a Linux developer workstation: a reviewer re-running the mutation check finds `sandbox-exec: command not found`, so the described RED-under-mutation verification cannot be reproduced on that platform.
Platform=Windows: no sandbox-exec and no POSIX shell, same non-reproducibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sandbox-exec-specific instruction with a portable equivalent: re-introduce WAIT_AND_RETRY into the failover set and assert `pytest tests/unit/test_throttle_no_failover_1c0d.py` goes RED, then restore — no macOS-only binary required.

Plan quote: 'RETRY_NOW (a down local endpoint, the case cross-provider failover genuinely exists for) … STILL fail over' — reframes RETRY_NOW as the only genuine failover case, silently dropping the 529/5xx-overload failover the chain was built for (test file docstring lines 3-4: 'a provider being throttled')
findings.finding: The fix excludes the ENTIRE WAIT_AND_RETRY disposition from failover, but that disposition also covers a persistently overloaded/unavailable primary (HTTP 529 / 5xx / read-timeout per failure.py:_map_http and the httpx.TimeoutException arm), not just the account-throttle 429 that motivated the change. Removing failover for those cases narrows the pre-existing 'a throttled/overloaded provider fails over' contract (pinned today at test_llm_fallback_chain.py:449-450 for 529/503) beyond the reported root cause, so a genuinely-down primary with a credential-reachable fallback would no longer fail over.
findings.location: Fix plan (Phase 2 — Direction C.c1); AC line 'should_fall_back returns False for a WAIT_AND_RETRY failure (plain 429 / 529 overloaded / read-timeout)'
scenarios: Bedrock primary returns sustained 529/503 (provider-side overload, not an account throttle) while a credential-reachable fallback provider is configured and healthy: after the change the chain retries the primary and surfaces exit-11 instead of failing over to the reachable provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) add a positive rationale in the plan for why 529/5xx-overload and read-timeouts should also stop failing over (e.g. because the real fallback in the frontier chain is keyless and the transport already retries), and update the test-file docstring's 'a provider being throttled fails over' framing to match; or (b) scope the exclusion to the specific 429 rate-limit case (leaving 529/5xx failover intact) if cross-provider failover on primary overload is still desired.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a positive rationale for narrowing should_fall_back over the credential-reachable-fallback guard named in the attribution (which would close the keyless-fallback masking for RETRY_NOW/CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL too), or adopt the guard if it is defensibly superior on robustness.
evidence: Plan quote (Attribution): 'its plan enabled cross-provider failover on a retryable throttle without a credential-reachable-fallback guard'

The chosen fix operates on the disposition set (should_fall_back), not on fallback-candidate reachability — so a keyless fallback still masks failover for RETRY_NOW/CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL classes, which continue to fail over into the same keyless anthropic:opus
findings.finding: The plan attributes the defect to '8fbd's plan enabling cross-provider failover on a retryable throttle WITHOUT a credential-reachable-fallback guard', which names a structurally-different alternative at the failover boundary (gate failover on the fallback candidate's credential being reachable) that would fix the reported masking directly while preserving throttle/overload failover to a reachable provider. The plan does not state why the broader predicate-narrowing was chosen over the credential-guard alternative its own attribution identifies.
scenarios: A RETRY_NOW (httpx.ConnectError on a down local primary) or CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL failover still routes to the keyless anthropic:opus fallback and re-raises the same bare TypeError→NEEDS_INVESTIGATION→INDETERMINATE the plan is fixing — because the fix only removes WAIT_AND_RETRY from the failover set, not the keyless-fallback masking mechanism.
